214.summary: Humphreys can account for Spain's wavering over the Spanish minister Yrujo's recall only by supposing that Yrujo shares, with certain lea[d?][ing?] [men?] at Madrid, in the profits of an exclusive [trade?] from the United States to the Spanish colonies; asks whether to stay at Lisbon or go home if forced to leave Spain; tells Urquijo of his own belief that France had {never} given up its design on Louisiana ("re[197][1355]ished", read as "relinquished", is mostly guessed), and reports Urquijo's assurance that France {should} {never} get it while he remained in office.

188.summary: The Swedish chargé at Madrid (from the enclosures) gave Humphreys reason to believe (the reading, word for word) "that the government of [Sweden?] {now} less [inclin?]d to use management with that of France ... and that it is even probable the Baron [935] sta[ël?] would soon retire from Paris"; fills the asterisks in Naval Documents, Quasi-War 2:437.

0364.summary: Humphreys has seen a letter from the Dutch minister at Paris reporting (in clear) the outcry against Scherer's peculations and Rewbell's leaving the Directory with thirty millions.

snip.cap: No. 188, 19 March 1799: the 56 code groups after “This Gentleman”
snip.credit: National Archives (NARA), RG 59, Despatches from U.S. Ministers to Spain, vol. 4, microfilm M31 roll 5, frame 0294, via the National Archives Catalog

system: One-part scrambled numerical code of about 1,600 elements (numbers 2-1590 seen) for words, syllables, single letters and punctuation, with a few homophones: Jefferson's 'Code No. 8' of 1785 (Boyd), Weber's unlocated '994 = the' code.
